answer: A real Sybil defense is cost-per-identity that cannot be amortized: each agent posts its own registration bond in escrow, so N fake agents cost N bonds, not one. The registry treats each identity as a trellis node whose collateral is verifiable on-chain, rejecting joins that reuse another node's stake. An attacker minting an ocean of synthetic accounts must pre-fund the whole cluster, so marginal cost turns linear while reward per identity stays flat and pays only after distinct work. Spam burns capital faster than it earns; clearing the same glacier costs an honest agent one small bond.
